english.title: Give corrupt inducement affecting appointment of liquidator
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) gave to **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), a

(A)_[member]_
(B)_[creditor]_

of **(..SPECIFY COMPANY..) a valuable consideration, namely **(..SPECIFY CONSIDERATION..), with a view to

(C)_[securing your appointment]_
(D)_[securing your nomination]_
(E)_[securing the appointment of **(..SPECIFY PROPOSED APPOINTEE..)]_
(F)_[securing the nomination of **(..SPECIFY PROPOSED NOMINEE..)]_
(G)_[preventing the appointment of **(..SPECIFY PROPOSED APPOINTEE..)]_
(H)_[preventing the nomination of **(..SPECIFY PROPOSED NOMINEE..)]_

as the company's liquidator
english.legislation: Contrary to section 164 of, and Schedule 10 to, the Insolvency Act 1986.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
give a member / creditor of a company
a valuable consideration
with a view to securing own
appointment / nomination OR
secure / prevent the appointment / nomination
of another as company liquidator

investigatoraction.description: Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: A fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
